open_points.subject: owner channel and personal-data isolation
open_points.text: “the only reader of personal data. Reaches the kernel through the agent channel with the owner's token” and “An agent never receives a `personal_data` value”
open_points.question: How does an owner receive personal-data values through the agent channel without exposing those values or the owner's token to the language-model agent?
options: The owner is a distinct MCP client
The channel separates owner-only UI responses from agent context
An agent relays owner requests but cannot inspect protected responses
open_points.default_guess: Use a distinct authenticated owner session whose protected responses are never placed in agent context.

open_points.subject: platform manifest authority
open_points.text: “Microservices — known only as records of the platform manifest”
open_points.question: Who creates and changes the platform manifest, how does the kernel obtain it, and why may its operation records and instance selections be trusted?
options: Owner-managed signed file
Installation-managed trusted configuration
Manifest service with authenticated reads
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as owner-controlled installation configuration loaded from a protected local file.

open_points.subject: MCP transport boundary
open_points.text: “one inbound channel, `mcp`, behind the host's reverse proxy”
open_points.question: Which MCP transport and request-authentication mechanism constitute the inbound channel, and which proxy-provided facts, if any, does the kernel trust?
options: Streamable HTTP with bearer tokens
SSE-based MCP with bearer tokens
Local stdio exposed through a host adapter
open_points.default_guess: Use Streamable HTTP behind the proxy and have the kernel validate bearer tokens itself.

open_points.subject: withheld secret-bearing service response
open_points.text: “A service's own answer that echoes one verbatim is withheld”
open_points.question: What observable node and run result occurs when a response contains a configured secret: refusal, failed validation, redacted output, or another result?
options: Fail the node and record a secret-detected reason
Redact the matching value and continue
Withhold the entire response and end the run
open_points.default_guess: Fail the node, expose no response value, and record a non-secret diagnostic reason.

open_points.subject: submission of outside material
open_points.text: “Their material stays at a microservice's own intake until the owner or an agent submits it”
open_points.question: Which kernel action submits an intake item, what reference and metadata it accepts, and what output or refusal it produces?
options: It is a normal run input containing an intake-record reference
There is a separate submit-intake action
An operation node selects intake material without caller submission
open_points.default_guess: Treat the intake-record reference as a typed input to `run a flow`, with the submitting principal recorded on the run.

open_points.subject: scope of the may-author right
open_points.text: “the token says whether the agent may author”, while “compose and prove a flow” and “propose an operation binding” name any agent
open_points.question: Does `may-author` gate flow composition and binding proposals as well as function contracts, implementations and trial cases?
options: It gates every persistent design artifact
It gates only function and trial artifacts
Each artifact type has separate rights
open_points.default_guess: Gate every action that creates a persistent function, trial, flow or binding artifact.

open_points.subject: flow-run inputs
open_points.text: “run a flow | owner, agent | a run of the flow's active version”
open_points.question: What inputs does starting a run accept, how are the flow's external input ports identified, and what happens when an input is missing, extra, wrongly typed or wrongly classified?
options: Named values validated before a run is created
Positional values validated before a run is created
Create a failed run for invalid inputs
open_points.default_guess: Accept named values for declared flow-input ports and refuse before creating a run if validation fails.

open_points.subject: trial case oracle
open_points.text: “add a trial case” and “the trial case every later implementation must pass”
open_points.question: What does a trial case contain and what exactly constitutes passing it: an exact expected output, schema conformance, an expected failure, predicates, or something else?
options: Inputs plus exact expected outputs
Inputs whose execution need only succeed and satisfy output schemas
Inputs plus declarative output assertions
open_points.default_guess: Use inputs plus exact canonical expected outputs and require successful contract-conforming execution.

open_points.subject: capturing a failed execution
open_points.text: “capture a failed execution into the trial corpus”
open_points.question: Because a failed execution may have no correct output, who supplies the expected result or assertion needed to turn it into a trial case?
options: The capturing actor supplies expected outputs
Capture only the inputs and require future success
The kernel derives an expected failure assertion
open_points.default_guess: Require the capturing actor to provide the expected output or explicit assertion.

open_points.subject: try versus automatic admission
open_points.text: “try an implementation” and “admit and activate | kernel, when an implementation is submitted”
open_points.question: Does authoring an implementation automatically run the whole corpus and admit or activate it, or must an agent first invoke `try`; and what does explicitly trying an already stored implementation change?
options: Submission automatically tries, admits and activates
Try is required before admission
Submission performs admission while `try` is a non-mutating preview
open_points.default_guess: Submission automatically runs admission over the corpus; `try` is a non-mutating preview that records trial evidence but does not activate.

open_points.subject: approval target and result
open_points.text: “approve or refuse an effect | owner | the effect runs on the exact input shown”
open_points.question: How does the owner identify one exact waiting attempt when several exist, and what result is returned when the approved send is unreachable or has an unknown outcome rather than demonstrably running?
options: Target an effect-attempt ID and return its new state
Target run plus node and return the run state
Only one approval may be outstanding per run
open_points.default_guess: Target an immutable effect-attempt ID and return whether it was sent, remains awaiting, became unreachable, or became outcome-unknown.

open_points.subject: standing-grant eligibility
open_points.text: “a `destructive` node or a version that is not active cannot be granted”, while K-08 applies grants only to nodes that stop for approval
open_points.question: May standing grants be created for `read` or `draft-write` nodes, which never normally stop for approval, or only for `state-transition` and `external-effect` nodes?
options: Only state-transition and external-effect
Every class except destructive
Every effectful class except destructive
open_points.default_guess: Permit grants only for `state-transition` and `external-effect` nodes.

open_points.subject: reading a trace
open_points.text: “read a trace | owner, agent | trace records | —”
open_points.question: What happens when the requested run or trace does not exist, is malformed, or is not visible to the caller?
options: Return unknown reference
Return an empty result
Use the general inspect action instead
open_points.default_guess: Refuse with `unknown reference`, applying the normal disclosure transformation to returned records.

open_points.subject: actions absent from the fixed MCP surface
open_points.text: “one fixed set of typed operations over `mcp`: inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel”
open_points.question: Which MCP operations expose adding trial cases, capturing failed executions, releasing failed runs, rolling back slots, proposing bindings, and composing or proving flows?
options: They are distinct omitted MCP operations
They are subcommands of `author`
Some are automatic and have no callable operation
open_points.default_guess: Expose them as explicitly typed variants under `author`, except release and rollback, which should be distinct operations.

open_points.subject: effect-class declaration
open_points.text: “Effect classes are `read`, `draft-write`, `state-transition`, `external-effect`, `destructive`”
open_points.question: Where is an operation's effect class declared, who is authorized to choose it, and what prevents an agent from binding an effectful operation as `read`?
options: The trusted manifest operation record declares it
The owner assigns it while accepting a binding
The kernel derives it from the HTTP method
open_points.default_guess: Require the trusted manifest operation record to declare the class and prevent bindings from overriding it.

open_points.subject: value-schema system
open_points.text: “Every port carries a value schema. An edge is valid when both ports carry the same schema.”
open_points.question: What schema language and canonical equality rule define “the same schema”, and which validation rules apply at runtime?
options: Canonical JSON Schema subset
A kernel-defined closed type algebra
Byte-identical stored schema documents
open_points.default_guess: Use a closed kernel-defined type algebra with canonical serialization and structural equality.

open_points.subject: function execution interface
open_points.text: “A function node runs one admitted implementation of one contract: declared input in, declared output out”
open_points.question: What Python entry point, input/output serialization, file-port interface and error protocol must an implementation obey?
options: A fixed callable receiving and returning typed objects
JSON over standard input/output plus mounted file paths
A generated wrapper around a named function
open_points.default_guess: Use a fixed callable contract with JSON-compatible value arguments and explicit read-only input/write-only output file handles.

open_points.subject: resource bounds
open_points.text: “declared input in, declared output out” and “typed ports and resource bounds”
open_points.question: Which resources can contracts bound, in what units and ranges, and how is each exceeded bound reported during trials and real runs?
options: Time, memory, output bytes and process count with fixed units
A kernel-wide fixed profile only
Per-contract profiles selected from a closed catalog
open_points.default_guess: Use a closed catalog of bounded time, memory, output bytes and process-count profiles, with a sandbox-violation failure naming the exceeded resource.

open_points.subject: map execution semantics
open_points.text: “a map of a node over a collection”
open_points.question: How are collection order, per-item identities, concurrency, partial failures, output ordering and effect approvals defined for a mapped node?
options: Sequential ordered map that fails affected items
Parallel map preserving input order
All-or-nothing map
open_points.default_guess: Execute in stable input order, create a distinct node execution per item, preserve output order and apply ordinary dependency failure per item.

open_points.subject: guard execution semantics
open_points.text: “a guard on a declared closed value”
open_points.question: What does a guard compare, how are its branches represented and proven, and what outputs and trace statuses result for the branch not taken?
options: Equality against one enum value with skipped-node traces
Switch over all members of a closed enum
Boolean guard only
open_points.default_guess: Use equality against a declared enum member, execute one branch, and record non-selected nodes as skipped without outputs.

open_points.subject: flow interface declaration
open_points.text: “A flow's own inputs and outputs are values, never files”
open_points.question: How does a flow version declare which graph ports are its external inputs and outputs, their schemas, disclosure classes and requiredness?
options: Explicit named interface ports in the flow version
Infer unconnected ports from the graph
Use dedicated input and output nodes
open_points.default_guess: Store explicit named input and output port declarations in every flow version.

open_points.subject: execution order of independent nodes
open_points.text: “A flow is an immutable, acyclic graph” and “A failed node stops only its dependants”
open_points.question: Are independent ready nodes run sequentially or concurrently, and what deterministic ordering governs approvals and externally visible operation sends?
options: Stable sequential topological order
Concurrent execution with deterministic trace ordering
Concurrent reads but sequential effects
open_points.default_guess: Run ready pure and read nodes concurrently but serialize effectful operation nodes in a stable topological order.

open_points.subject: idempotency-key semantics
open_points.text: “The kernel supplies the declared idempotency key”
open_points.question: Where is the key declared in an operation request, how is its value generated and stored, and is the same or a new key used after unreachable service, unknown-outcome resolution or an approved resend?
options: One stable key per node execution and all retries
A new key for every authorized send
Manifest-defined scope with kernel-generated value
open_points.default_guess: Let the manifest declare the request location and use one persisted key per logical effect attempt, retaining it across exact retries and approved resends.

open_points.subject: transport-outcome classification
open_points.text: “when a service is unreachable or an outcome unknown”
open_points.question: Which connection, timeout, protocol and response-validation outcomes count as safely unsent/unreachable, outcome-unknown, or definitively failed, especially for effects?
options: Classify by whether request bytes may have reached the service
Treat every timeout as outcome-unknown for effects
Require service-specific transport declarations
open_points.default_guess: Use transport evidence: before-send failures are unreachable, any failure after sending may be outcome-unknown for effects, and definitive HTTP or validation responses are failed.

open_points.subject: aggregate run status
open_points.text: “resume a run ... whatever else the run waits for” and “A run rests `awaiting_approval`, or `pending`”
open_points.question: What single run status is reported when different independent nodes simultaneously await approval, await service reachability, have unknown outcomes or have failed?
options: Define a precedence among aggregate statuses
Represent multiple simultaneous wait reasons
Disallow more than one kind of wait at a time
open_points.default_guess: Keep a set of active wait reasons and derive a documented display status with outcome-unknown first, then unreachable, then awaiting approval.

open_points.subject: cancelling an unknown-outcome run
open_points.text: “only the owner's resolution moves it” and “cancel a run | owner | the run ends `cancelled`”
open_points.question: May the owner cancel a run whose effect outcome is still unknown, and if so how is the permanently unresolved attempt represented after the run ends?
options: Allow cancellation while preserving an unresolved attempt
Refuse cancellation until the outcome is resolved
Cancellation implicitly resolves it as not applied
open_points.default_guess: Allow cancellation but preserve the effect attempt permanently as outcome-unknown; cancellation must not imply an outcome.

open_points.subject: trace and effect-attempt record granularity
open_points.text: “Every node execution writes one immutable trace record” and “inspect ... effect attempts”
open_points.question: Are retries, resumptions, mapped items, approval waits and sends separate immutable node-execution or effect-attempt records, and how are they linked to one logical node?
options: One trace per attempt plus separate effect-attempt records
One append-only event stream per logical node
One immutable summary created only when the node finishes
open_points.default_guess: Store one immutable record per execution attempt and a distinct effect-attempt record, linked by run, logical node and attempt number.

open_points.subject: bounded value and trace limits
open_points.text: “bounded values that edges carry” and “Traces carry no secret and no unbounded payload”
open_points.question: What limits apply to values, outputs and trace fields, and what observable failure occurs when a service or function exceeds them?
options: Fixed installation-wide byte limits
Schema-declared limits enforced at ports
Store only digests after a fixed inline threshold
open_points.default_guess: Require schemas and contracts to state byte limits, reject oversized port values, and store only bounded metadata plus digests in traces.

open_points.subject: repair-context access
open_points.text: “For repair an agent receives one contract, its current implementation and that slot's recent traces and trial evidence”
open_points.question: Which action declares that an agent is repairing a slot, what author right is required to receive implementation code, and what deterministic rule defines “recent” traces?
options: A dedicated get-repair-context action
A mode of inspect restricted to authoring agents
Automatically supplied after a failed run
open_points.default_guess: Provide a dedicated author-only repair-context query returning the latest bounded number of relevant traces plus all active trial evidence.

open_points.subject: classification of no-input function outputs
open_points.text: “a function's output takes the highest class its execution received”
open_points.question: What disclosure class is assigned when a function has no inputs, or when it produces a value independent of all received inputs?
options: Default to `open`
Require a declared minimum output class
Forbid functions with no inputs
open_points.default_guess: Require each function output to declare a minimum class and take the maximum of that class and all received input classes.

open_points.subject: external photo processing
open_points.text: “the agent processes a photo itself, outside the kernel” and “a caller never hands the kernel a file and never receives one”
open_points.question: Which named external system gives the agent access to the photo and runs its processing, and how can that happen without violating the rule that agents receive personal data only as digest and class?
options: The agent uses a microservice operation without receiving the file
Only the owner processes the photo outside the kernel
Photo processing is removed from the acceptance path
open_points.default_guess: Have a declared microservice operation process the photo while the agent receives only references, digests and permitted analysis values.

open_points.subject: photo acceptance pending state
open_points.text: “it shows effect classes, the owner's approval on the exact input, the idempotency key and `pending`”
open_points.question: Which deliberate event must produce `pending` in the photo case—an unreachable service or an unknown effect outcome—and what subsequent resolution or resume must the case demonstrate?
options: Simulated outcome-unknown followed by owner resolution
Simulated unreachable service followed by resume
Both pending reasons in separate bounded variants
open_points.default_guess: Demonstrate both reasons separately: unreachable followed by resume, and outcome-unknown followed by owner resolution.

open_points.subject: negative acceptance coverage
open_points.text: “each refusal of K-05 through K-09 is shown by a bounded negative case”
open_points.question: Does “each refusal” mean one case per decision, every explicitly listed refusal and failure branch, or every distinct refusal code later introduced?
options: Every distinct normative refusal path
One representative case for each of K-05 through K-09
Only refusals named in the Primary actions table
open_points.default_guess: Require one bounded case for every distinct normative refusal or failure path stated in K-05 through K-09.

open_points.subject: third-party analysis acceptance
open_points.text: “Within one conversation ... returns an analysis, releasing nothing.”
open_points.question: What defines one conversation, who receives the analysis, what facts make the analysis correct, and does “releasing nothing” mean no effects, no files, no confidential disclosure, or all of these?
options: A scripted MCP session with expected analysis values and no effect nodes
A human-reviewed conversation transcript
A run-level test asserting no outbound writes or protected disclosures
open_points.default_guess: Define a scripted MCP session whose owner-visible expected analysis values match fixtures and whose trace contains no effectful operation or protected-data disclosure.
